answer: A signal is worthless if the sender cannot be separated from the crowd. Each identity needs two holders outside its own knoll to countersign its transmission, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct signers rather than one ring. Every transmission is priced by rank: the k-th filing costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still requiring unrelated guarantors. A ripple audit replays a random transmission each epoch, and an unconfirmed one voids the knoll and forfeits its bond, which cannot be resold.
